name: Abutilon

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Start at the flower center and mature fruit, not leaf color. Check whether the staminal column is hairy, count the style branches when visible, then inspect fruit size and whether mericarp tips are merely acute/apiculate or form long divergent spines.
shared_traits: Alternate cordate leaves with stellate pubescence
Five-petaled mallow flowers with stamens united into a staminal column
Dry schizocarp made of persistent mericarps
shared_genus_recognition.caution: Leaf hairiness and yellow flowers overlap. Reproductive structures are more reliable than overall grayness or flower color.

species_comparison_matrix.incanum: Subshrub 1–2 m; ovate-cordate leaves to ~6 cm, densely tomentulose
species_comparison_matrix.theophrasti: Annual herb to 1+ m; very large broadly ovate/suborbiculate leaves 8–15 cm

species_comparison_matrix.incanum: Yellow or pink with dark red center; petals 4–6 mm; corolla reflexed

species_comparison_matrix.weight: BEST FRUTICOSUM VS INCANUM FLOWER CHARACTER

species_comparison_matrix.incanum: 3–5 mm; lobes spreading or somewhat reflexed in fruit

overlap_cautions: A. fruticosum and A. incanum both have small cordate hairy leaves and compact cask-shaped fruits; use staminal-column pubescence plus style count.
Flower color helps but is not sufficient by itself.
A. theophrasti fruit is dramatically larger and long-spined; it should not be confused with the two compact-fruited subshrubs once mature fruit is present.
Preserve current learner/native-range labels: A. fruticosum unresolved, A. incanum nonlocal comparison, A. theophrasti non-native comparison.

local_lookalikes.separate: Compare mericarp form and style number.
Compare leaves, calyx and fruit segments.
Furled corolla and fleshy fruit differ from dry Abutilon fruit.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.show: staminal column surface + style branches, with arrows/count labels
diagnostic_photo_checklist.separates: pubescent 5-style incanum vs glabrous 6–9-style fruticosum vs 13–15-style theophrasti

diagnostic_photo_checklist.show: schizocarp diameter/height with ruler and mericarp tips
diagnostic_photo_checklist.separates: compact acute/apiculate fruticosum/incanum from large long-spined theophrasti

diagnostic_photo_checklist.show: flower front and side at similar scale
diagnostic_photo_checklist.separates: plain yellow fruticosum from often dark-centered/reflexed incanum

diagnostic_photo_checklist.show: blade + petiole with scale and surface texture
diagnostic_photo_checklist.separates: huge velvetleaf foliage; supporting only for fruticosum/incanum

handoffs.question: Verify additional calyx, mericarp-apex and style-count thresholds from authoritative keys before making a strict dichotomous key.
Find matched licensed flower-center and mature fruit macros; retain photo provenance.

curation_status.visual_status: diagnostic matrix complete; reproductive gallery improved; matched flower-center macros still open
curation_status.scientific_note: FNA-backed morphology pass; no range/admission changes.

field_key_training.if: Large ~15 × 20 mm wheel/crown with many 3–6 mm divergent spines
Staminal column visibly pubescent and style divides into 5 branches
field_key_training.then: A. incanum strongly supported; dark-centered/reflexed corolla adds support.

field_key_training.if: Staminal column glabrous and style has 6–9 branches
field_key_training.then: A. fruticosum strongly supported; plain yellow flower and 8–9 mm cask-shaped fruit confirm.

field_key_training.if: Large velvety 8–15 cm leaves on an annual
field_key_training.then: A. theophrasti is plausible; otherwise wait for flowers/fruit before separating fruticosum and incanum.
